findings.property: the framework unit gate result depends only on the tests, not on how many bytes earlier tests leave in the bounded /tmp tmpfs
findings.severity: low: fail-safe (the unit gate FAILs with ENOSPC, never a false PASS), but one added test that leaves a few small files in /tmp can fail an unrelated foundation test, so the gate is fragile and the failure points at the wrong test
findings.rationale: At d2b2ebe the unit gate passed with 1,498 tests (check-fast 9c364e52). At 5a7ae77 and 3b5fcf5 Task DD added 4 framework tests (SharedCheckFileTests) that left about 20 small files in mkdtemp directories; test_foundation then failed twice with OSError ENOSPC while it copied the foundation inputs into a TemporaryDirectory (first a schema file, then the glib callback-ABI patch). At 632e697 the 4 tests remove their directories (addCleanup) and the gate passes again (check-fast 883677ce, 17/17 PASS, 1,502 tests). So earlier tests leave nearly 64 MiB minus 9.5 MiB in /tmp, and the remaining margin is a few hundred KiB at most. Not measured: which tests leave the bytes, and how many. Repair options (not done): remove temporary directories in the tests that leave them, or give the unit job its own scratch; a change of tmp_bytes is a protected runtime-setting change. Owner: framework release coordinator. Phase: independent authority (a tmp_bytes change is a protected runtime setting; a test cleanup needs no ruling).

findings.location: benchmarks/performance/python/tests/test_native_kernel.py, test_native_worker.py, test_native_inproc.py swap tests; benchlab/native_worker.py confirm_verified (unchanged at the repair commit 2bd4792; since FR12 it compares st_dev and st_ino of the path with the verified descriptor, and _identity with st_ctime_ns stays as an extra signal)
findings.property: the verified-start swap tests give the same result in every run
findings.severity: low: a test result depended on the coarse timestamp tick; no unverified file ran in either outcome
findings.rationale: Cause (before FR12): os.replace over the verified path drops the link count of the verified inode and so changes its ctime. confirm_verified compared (dev, inode, size, mtime, ctime) after the start, so it refused (changed) when the coarse clock of file timestamps ticked between the hash and the swap, and let the verified file run when it did not. This was a timing dependence of the code under test, not a security race: in both outcomes the swapped file never ran (the start is from the verified descriptor, and a refusal reaps it). At the repair commit 2bd4792 the code was unchanged (the ctime check detects a write followed by an mtime reset). The tests were repaired, with no assertion weakened and no retry: the swap-not-started tests swapped the directory that holds the file (the verified inode was untouched, so the verified file ran, as asserted before; the kernel test also asserted that the swapped file never ran), and a new test per route renames over the file after an explicit condition (the coarse clock is past the ctime) and asserts the refusal (changed). Evidence class (FR7b-R1-01): a corrected test expectation, not the same regression failing before and passing after. The reproducer expected the verified kernel to run after the tick; the fixed test expects a refusal (changed) on the same input. The directory-swap tests were new inputs that kept the original assertions. Current state (since FR12, row FR7b-IDENTITY-RULE-01, owner rule: a replaced file is always refused): confirm_verified also compares st_dev and st_ino of the path with the verified descriptor, so the result no longer depends on the clock. The directory-swap tests now expect the refusal (changed), and the swapped file never runs. The start through the descriptor is asserted by the unchanged-kernel test (executable /proc/self/fd/N) and by the worker test test_the_descriptor_is_closed_in_the_caller_after_the_start. The tick tests are unchanged and still pass.
findings.reproducer: bench selftest unit run 471b2b02, test test_a_kernel_swapped_after_the_hash_is_not_started; deterministic reproducer in bench unit run 2009af12

findings.location: benchmarks/performance/python/benchlab/native_worker.py _identity, confirm_verified (used by the worker, kernel and inproc verified starts: NativeWorker.start, native_kernel._start, native_inproc.load)
findings.property: the verified-start identity rule gives one outcome for a rename over a verified file, or the variance is accepted by the independent authority
findings.severity: low: the ctime re-check makes the outcome of a rename over the verified path depend on a timestamp tick (refused or run); both outcomes are safe, because the swapped file never runs
findings.rationale: For the independent authority: keep the rule (ctime detects a write followed by an mtime reset) and accept the variance, or change the rule (for example compare ctime only with an unchanged link count) with its own threat review. Owner: framework release coordinator. Phase: before release qualification closes. No code change without that ruling. FR12 ruling (owner decision of 2026-10-16): a replaced file is always refused. confirm_verified(fd, sha256, identity, path) now compares st_dev and st_ino of lstat(path) with those of fstat on the verified descriptor at the check point; any difference, or a path that no longer exists, refuses with 'changed', independent of any clock. The ctime check stays as an extra signal (a write followed by an mtime reset); it is never the only signal. The same path identity rule already holds in the restore check of the native job (container/bench_native_job.py _still_verified). Consequence of the rule: a swap of the directory that holds the file now refuses as well (at the check point the path names another file), so the three directory-swap tests now expect the refusal, and each asserts that the swapped file never runs: the kernel test finds no marker of the swapped file; the worker test finds that the started process runs the interpreter of the verified peer (not /bin/sh of the swapped file) and no marker, and that the process is refused and reaped (FR12-A01); the inproc test finds that the loader saw only the verified bytes. The tick tests stay; the new tests cover the same refusal more strongly: a rename over with no clock wait, and a rename over with the ctime signal removed (the no-tick case made deterministic), for each route. The new unchanged-file tests pass (the kernel test also asserts the start from /proc/self/fd/N).
findings.reproducer: benchmarks/performance/python/tests test_native_kernel.py, test_native_worker.py, test_native_inproc.py: the renamed_over_is_refused_with_no_clock_wait and renamed_over_is_refused_when_the_ctime_gives_no_signal tests, the directory-swap tests and the unchanged-file tests

findings.location: tools/project_image.py build_image (added-bytes check) and admit (cache count)
findings.property: a project bench image is admitted only when the owned-image bounds of safety/container-policy.json hold
findings.severity: low: the count bound is exact (max_owned_images over both cache kinds), but the byte bound of a new project bench image is a projection: its image Size minus the developer image Size must be at most two times the payload bytes plus one 4 KiB block per file, plus 1 MiB for the image metadata and directory entries (the fixture image measured 43,211 added bytes for 1,851 payload bytes in 5 files). The exact measurement of the developer assembler (owned_image_bytes over unique containerd snapshots and content blobs) is not applied, so the total bytes of all owned images are not checked when a project image is built. The layer itself is bounded (192 MiB, 3072 files), so the excess is bounded per image
findings.rationale: Recorded with the EX-1 design, no fix in this task: the exact measurement streams docker image save of every owned image and is part of the pinned developer assembler, which a change of recipe would requalify. Proposed fix for an independent decision: move the exact measurement into a shared helper and apply it to the project bench build, with FR4-IMG-BOUND-01. Owner: framework release coordinator. Phase: with FR4-IMG-BOUND-01 (the next developer image requalification).
findings.reproducer: tests/unit/test_project_image.py ImageBuildTests.test_too_many_added_bytes_remove_the_new_image proves the projection only; no test measures the total owned bytes at a project image build

findings.location: .githooks/personal_info_check.py Scanner.project_pinned (the EX1-A03 route) and Scanner.content; schemas/project-third-party.json; tools/project_third_party.py check_lock, verify_files
findings.property: the privacy hook exempts the content of a file under a project's benchmarks/project/third_party/ directory only when the project lock of the same revision binds its exact path, sha256 and size in a row whose origin URL is on the upstream allowlist; names, the lock itself and every unbound file get every rule; a bound path with other bytes is a finding
findings.severity: medium: the hook pinned only wheel parts under third_party/wheels/ with a PyPI origin, so a project could not commit its upstream notices and provenance records (upstream author emails), an upstream source archive or retained upstream headers (email-address, unpinned-archive); a bound file with other bytes was no finding of its own. The gap failed closed: no personal value could pass
findings.rationale: Additive lock forms: retained rows (upstream files kept without their archive), files of a wheel or source row, and an optional size of a provenance or notice record; check_lock applies the name and path rules to them and refuses a row that binds the lock itself; verify_files checks every byte. One hook route for every bound file: a row with an allowlisted origin (PyPI files, GitHub release downloads and archives, Boost release archives; UPSTREAM_URL equals the schema's $defs.exempt_origin_url) and the exact path, sha256 and size; under third_party/wheels/ only the EX1-A03 and EX1-R1-02 wheel rule; a project area nested in another one pins nothing; a bound path with other bytes is project-lock-mismatch. Residuals in the hook threat model: the lock of the same revision decides (a lock edit in the same commit passes, so the approver review of the protected directory is the control) and the allowlist checks the URL text only. Owner: framework release coordinator. FIX1 (approver finding T4-A09): the fix round 1 of this row (approver findings T4-A02 to T4-A05) is the row FW-HOOK-02, recorded through the ledger rules instead of a second attempt on this VERIFIED row; since that round a project lock counts only in a project root, so the property above holds inside project roots (T4-A11).

findings.location: ci/changed-examples commit_view, scope_problems and main; tools/project_model.py example_scopes; .github/workflows/example.yml select; ci/README.md
findings.property: A pull request that changes only examples/ skips safety.yml, so the example.yml select step fails closed for framework content under examples/: at the head, starter-export.json lists every file of a framework example tree, of an examples/<name> without project.json and directly under examples/, and lists no missing examples/ file; an examples/<name> of both base and head keeps its scope (framework, standalone, project-less) unless the change also changes starter-export.json (a pull request that changes it runs safety.yml). A head that git cannot read and a checkout whose standalone examples differ from those of the head give exit 2.
findings.severity: medium: before the repair a pull request that changed only examples/ could add an unlisted file to a framework example tree, a C file to an examples/<name> without project.json, or change the scope of an examples/<name>, with green GitHub checks; the next full ci then failed the inventory gate or B18 on an unrelated change. No false qualification: the local gates fail closed
findings.rationale: The paths-ignore rule examples/** of safety.yml leaves only the manifest check of example.yml, which sees the listed files only. The select step knows the base, the head and the changed paths, so it applies the export rules there; it reads both commits from git (ls-tree, and the export list through the capped JSON boundary) and names no example. Each scope change that passes the step changes starter-export.json, which safety.yml does not ignore. A push never starts safety.yml (unchanged design). The approver finding T3-A05 (LOW, coverage) is recorded in this row: the bounds of the commit id rule (39, 40, 41, 63, 64 and 65 hex digits, uppercase) and of the example name rule (64 and 65 characters, a leading dot, a non-ASCII name, the exit 2 branch) pass before and after (coverage only, not part of the attempt evidence).

findings.location: ci/changed-examples path_filter_problem, PATH_FILTER_LIMIT and the --event argument; .github/workflows/example.yml select (EVENT)
findings.property: With --event pull_request (example.yml passes github.event_name), the select step fails when a framework change has 300 or more changed paths or an unknown count, because GitHub evaluates the path filters of safety.yml over at most 300 files; a push (safety.yml has no push trigger) and a change of standalone examples only are not affected.
findings.severity: low: a pull request with more than 300 files could skip safety.yml unnoticed while a framework path changed; only ci/README.md documented the limit
findings.rationale: The count is git diff --no-renames of the base and the head commit (a rename counts twice), an approximation of the pull request diff of GitHub; the step fails at the limit itself to keep a margin. The remedy is to split the pull request. Without --event the script applies the push rule; the workflow test pins the --event line.
findings.reproducer: tests/unit/test_example_scope.py PathFilterLimitTests (299, 300 and 301 paths, an unknown count, a push, a standalone-only change, an unknown event) and TriggerDryRunTests.test_the_example_workflow_jobs (the EVENT lines of the select job)

In a project instance a run with the default project . needs bench selftest --project . (fail closed).

findings.property: H10: a local decision run measures its memory trials (one redacted container per memory trial, the memory item of the aggregate with the host memory.peak) and its capacity trials (percentiles inside the container), so a rule policy has the caller-scope group peaks of a local run

findings.origin: approver (EX-19 verdict finding T5-A05, LOW); new framework row
findings.location: tools/bench_evidence.py check_integrity (forged self-timing: |pyperf_wall_ns - wall_ns| > max(agreement_abs_ns, agreement_rel x wall_ns)); safety/performance-policy.json pyperf
findings.property: The pyperf agreement check of a Python kernel trial separates an integrity defect (the pyperf wall above the bracket wall: physically inconsistent) from the overhead of the bracket outside the pyperf region (the bracket above pyperf) at the 1 ms floor of a short trial; a check that fired is resolved by a finding, never by a re-run until PASS
findings.severity: low: a framework control smoke run of bench selftest cases (suite B17 in the fresh child ci of foundation selftest run 015355da, child run a631e9bb) was INVALID_EXPERIMENT with the reason forged self-timing: smoke-kernel-s01-b00-00: bracket wall_ns 31,650,646 ns, pyperf_wall_ns 30,580,927 ns, the bracket larger by 1,069,719 ns against the limit 1,000,000 ns (2 percent of the wall is 633,013 ns); fail closed (the run was invalid, nothing decided); pyperf did not exceed the bracket, so no integrity defect is shown; foundation selftest run d19a62de passed on a re-run
findings.rationale: The record was read by its two numeric fields from the archived child instance (evidence retention archive of the EX-19 check worktree). A re-run until PASS does not resolve a check that fired. Owner: framework release coordinator. Phase: task T7, before its full ci run (the full ci is not re-run until PASS on this check; a recurrence there is a finding of this row). Text correction (task T6-R1, finding T6-A01, ruling R18): the evidence of the bound counts 212 distinct honest trials (424 recorded rows, each kernel row stored twice); the old rule failed one distinct trial (recorded twice); the largest overhead, 1,661,031 ns, was on a 274.8 ms wall; the bound (3 x the largest) is unchanged. Coverage (task T6-R1, finding T6-A07): the live B15 case also rejects a self-timing far below its bracket (bench_phase3 b15_suite check forged-pyperf-wall-below, commit 35695ac); its first live run is the cases suite of the full ci of task T7.
findings.reproducer: the B17 smoke run of a framework control on a loaded host: a Python kernel trial of about 31 ms whose bracket exceeds the pyperf wall by more than 1 ms

findings.origin: approver (T5-R1 scoped re-review verdict, finding T5R1-A01, MEDIUM); new framework row
findings.location: container/bench-coordinator.py local_rule_counts (rule work-count, both loops; rule pool-identity); tools/bench.py check_completeness (P07) and check_concurrency_identity (B10); tools/bench_evidence.py check_integrity (wrong work count); tools/bench_plan.py b10_row_count
findings.property: A single-record (panel) trial is held to its planned work, len(panel) x panel_passes one-row calls (6 x L), never to the rows of its tier, by the host rules and the rules inside a local decision job alike (one definition, container/bench_trial_work.py); each pooled call of such a trial holds one row (B10); a dropped panel cell or pass, an extra call, zero work and the tier rows still break the rules
findings.severity: medium: every single-record trial broke the in-job rule work-count and the host rules P07 and B15 wrong work count, so every local window attempt and every synthetic run with a single-record unit was INVALID_EXPERIMENT (half of the owner units); fail closed, nothing was decided wrongly; a pooled single-record row of a non-tiny point also broke B10
findings.rationale: Found by reading (the T5-R1 approver; no recorded run held a panel observation). The planned work is defined once in a standard-library file that the host loads by its path and the coordinator imports, so the host and in-job rules cannot drift; the parity evidence (RuleTests) holds a single-record trial, clean and broken; the live bench unit suite checks a real single-record trial against the same definition.
findings.reproducer: tests/unit/test_bench_local_decision.py RuleTests (test_clean_evidence_breaks_no_rule_here_and_on_the_host with the single-record trial pn-b0, test_a_single_record_trial_breaks_no_work_rule_here_and_on_the_host, test_a_single_record_trial_with_other_work_breaks_the_work_rules_here_and_on_the_host, test_a_pooled_single_record_row_has_the_chunks_of_one_row_here_and_on_the_host) and PanelWorkTests; live: benchmarks/performance/python/tests/test_panel_trial.py test_the_work_rules_accept_a_real_single_record_trial

findings.rationale: Ruling R27: port the route of the former developer assembler (host streaming of declared oversized members, the separate 50331648-byte member bound) to the project layer as a generic, lock-declared route, before the framework qualification. Fixed in task T6-R2. No container policy, launcher or profile change; no other bound changed. Owner: framework stream.

findings.location: container/bench-coordinator.py REFERENCE_CODE, reference_path and job_reference (reference_selectors, check_reference_cover, reference_cover_file); tools/bench.py run_cmd (reference_selectors, reference_cover_ok); tools/bench_local_decision.py run_local_decision (job_reference_selectors); docs/performance-laboratory.md; benchmarks/performance/python/benchlab/workload.py
findings.property: the reference of a synthetic run, and of a local job whose trials hold more than one selector, covers the models of every planned selector: the job plan holds the sorted planned selectors (reference_selectors, only when a selector other than all is planned) and the adapter's optional hook reference_cover(data, selectors) returns one reference with one digest; an adapter without the hook keeps reference(data) of its reference selector, and without the list the reference child keeps its argv; a restored reference with a bound list, and a local job with a list, refuse a trial whose selector is outside it; the digest check of a restored reference is unchanged
findings.severity: medium: fail closed, but no decision was possible: a synthetic run computed one reference with selector all, so every caller row of a planned selector whose models are outside the all reference was ineligible for every variant (in the example: two of its five model selectors), and the local job of each window session (unit trials plus the control trials of selector all) had the same defect
findings.rationale: Task T6-R6, design (b) of the brief (one reference job, one digest): one reference per selector would compute the models of all a second time, while the hook makes the reference work grow only by the models of the planned selectors. The call deadline of the reference job still uses the shares of the call-deadline selectors (unchanged, ruling R51). The count hooks run on the adapter of the reference selector. Owner: framework stream.
findings.reproducer: tests/unit/test_bench_reference_cover.py SyntheticRunReferenceTests, NoCrossUseTests, HostRunTests and LocalJobReferenceTests (a stand-in adapter whose all selector computes two of four models; the caller rows of a third selector validate only through the hook)

findings.rationale: Task T6-R6. The derivation of a decision plan gives the same identities (its points are the case points); a dataset_ref that only an unplanned case point declares is now run-invalid in every mode. Owner: framework stream.
findings.reproducer: tests/unit/test_bench_windows.py PlannedPointDatasetTests (a window smoke plan, a unit smoke job plan and a window decision plan whose single-record unit point declares synthetic:large#panel; forged identities)

findings.origin: framework hit of demo run 34dc1922 of the standalone benchmark example (task T26, section Demo run 1 diagnosis: INVALID_EXPERIMENT, the warm single-record trials of one variant killed at their call deadline) and controller ruling R86; repaired in task T6-R7; new framework row
findings.source_identity: commit 884d99a (the framework head at the start of the round)
findings.location: tools/bench_plan.py calibration_inputs, measured_walls, call_class, panel_fields, panel_trial_estimate, caller_trial_estimate, measured_trial_seconds, route_budget, wall_probes, _probe_rows and build_plan; tools/bench_deadline.py measured_seconds, covering_deadline, deadline_fields and _stub_plan; tools/bench_windows.py trial_seconds and _control_seconds; tools/bench.py planned_points; docs/performance-laboratory.md section Plan sizing and calibration; tools/bench_plan.py PROBE_SMOKE_CAP_SECONDS (ruling R87)
findings.property: after calibration every caller-scope timing trial of a plan is sized from the measured wall of its variant, selector and call class (one-row or multi-row) of the calibration run, never from a per-family rate of multi-row all calls times a selector share: the passes L of a single-record trial, its expected wall, the input of its call deadline, and the session, memory, group, window and control estimates; a planned class without a measured wall refuses the plan (wall-not-measured, exit 1); the smoke plan measures every class that a decision plan of the case can hold (one probe point per selector and call class); a written plan binds the walls in its calibration and bench run --plan derives them again; each probe session starts with one untimed warmup trial of the same shape per variant (the same trial child), so the timed trial measures the steady wall without the one-time cost of a new child; a smoke plan with probe points keeps every session within the 600 s smoke job deadline and may take up to PROBE_SMOKE_CAP_SECONDS (1,200 s) in all (ruling R87)
findings.severity: medium: fail closed (the run was INVALID_EXPERIMENT), but no decision run was possible: the plan sized the warm single-record trial of a variant with a fixed per-call cost of about 0.94 s per one-row call at 2.37 ms per call (L = 36, a call deadline of 60 s for a trial of about 200 s), so each such trial was killed at its call deadline; a second covered selector had a margin of 1.31 only, the full-dataset sessions ran 1.4 to 5.7 times their estimates, and the window plans of the unit policy sized every variant except the reference variant the same way
findings.rationale: Task T6-R7, the design choice of item 1(d): the smoke measures every class and the plan never extrapolates (a refusal alone would refuse every decision plan of the example). Fix 1 measured the probes without a warmup; the integration proof showed that a new trial child pays a one-time cost on one of its first calls, so ruling R87 adds a warmup of the same shape to each probe and lets a smoke plan with probes take up to 1,200 s. Kernel trials and the jobs (reference, panel, check, validate) keep their rate inputs. Owner: framework stream.
findings.reproducer: tests/unit/test_bench_measured_walls.py SingleRecordTrialTests, MultiRowUnitTests, WindowEstimateTests, NoExtrapolationTests, ProbeBoundTests and WallTests (the synthetic window fixture with a one-row wall of 0.94 s, about 209 times the rate x share of its row)

findings.property: a single-record (panel) trial reports the caller phases of its interval as every other caller trial does: prepare, work and materialize (and pool_start of a cold pool) are the sums over its 6 x L timed calls, and the transport of a C trial is the sum of the transport time that the codec reports for each call (its statistics are reset before each call, so a call that reports none leaves the transport unknown); B08 keeps its rule for every C caller row, so the one-row probe rows of a smoke plan meet it
findings.severity: medium: B08 failed for every native example whose smoke plan holds a one-row probe on a panel (a regression of task T6-R7: the one-row probe points are single-record trials, and a single-record trial reported no phases), so the cases suite of such an example could not pass; no wall was wrong, only the phase split of the interval was missing
findings.rationale: Design choice (task T6-R9, brief item 2): a probe trial records the same phases as every other C trial, and no probe marker exists. The probe rows are measurements of the smoke run (the calibration reads their walls), and every single-record trial (the single-record unit rows of a decision run too) had the same gap, so a marker would have excused rows that the design covers (G7.1: the caller wall holds prepare, transport, work and materialize; the B08 rows of G12 and I12). B08 is not changed. The framework control case has no single-record probe, so the framework qualification did not see the defect.
findings.reproducer: run the smoke of a native example whose case has a single-record (panel) caller point with a selector, then B08 (bench selftest --suite cases with the example): every C one-row probe row failed with the interval misses prepare, transport, work, materialize (run 389fbba5)
